name: ElevenLabs
positioning: A voice AI company that offers a text-to-speech API and a studio, with a large voice library, many languages and voice cloning.

pricing.model: Per-character API pricing that depends on the model, plus monthly subscription plans that include a character allowance
pricing.headline: API list prices are quoted per 1,000 characters and differ by model
pricing.freeTier: A free plan with a small monthly character allowance
promotions: A promotional price on one newer model that ends on a stated date

voices.customVoiceOrCloning: Instant and professional voice cloning on paid plans

compatibility.note: It has its own request shape and SDKs.

licensing.commercialUse: Commercial use of generated audio is allowed on paid plans
licensing.attributionOrConditions: Free plan output requires attribution to the vendor

limits.perRequestCharacters: Up to 10,000 characters on some models and fewer on others
limits.concurrency: Concurrent request limits depend on the plan

compliance.note: The security page describes SOC 2 and GDPR; it does not mention HIPAA for the standard plans.

strengths.claim: Lists a large voice library across many languages, with cloning on paid plans
Documents WebSocket streaming for text that arrives in pieces
Supports SSML-style controls and pronunciation dictionaries in its documentation

limitations.claim: Per-request character limits differ by model, so long text has to be split
Free plan output carries an attribution requirement

stepsToMove: List the voice ids your application uses and note which are library voices and which are your own clones.
Download the audio you generated and want to keep, since clones and library voices stay with the vendor.
Export the pronunciation dictionaries you maintain, if any, so you can apply the same fixes in plain text.
Revoke the API keys you no longer need once traffic has moved.

bestFor: Teams that need a wide choice of voices and languages, voice cloning, and SSML-style control.
unknowns: Concurrency numbers for each plan were not listed on the public pages we reviewed.
Whether the attribution requirement applies to API use on the free plan was not clear.
